subject: Enclave-lane topology and segregation Q&A for SOC 2 evidence
messages:
From: Veridian Audit Team <audits@veridian.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: visual topology + segregation narrative for SOC 2

Hi Karthik and Kimberly,

Thanks for the packet you shared last week. Our SOC 2 reviewer asked for a concise visual that highlights the separation between control plane, data plane, and tenant enclaves for both Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they want: a single-page diagram with callouts for:
- Where tenant compute runs (Dedicated GPU pools vs Private VPCs)
- Control plane connectivity and payloads (what travels to the control plane)
- Egress chokepoints and filtering (per-tenant egress policy)
- KMS/HSM boundary for customer-managed keys (if present)

Can you provide a diagram and a short narrative (200-400 words) describing how the model routing and fallback works across tiers? Delivery by EOD Tuesday (US) would keep us on track.

Attachments: none yet.

Thanks,
Ruth Allen
Veridian Audit Team
Ruth.Allen@veridian.com

--
Veridian Security Services
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Veridian Audit Team <audits@veridian.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: visual topology + segregation narrative for SOC 2

Ruth — thanks for the clear ask. We'll produce a one-page visual and a short narrative. A couple quick clarifying points to make sure we hit the right level of detail:
1) For "tenant compute" do you want us to show both the hosted (Redwood-hosted) Dedicated GPU pool and customer-managed Private VPC side-by-side, or focus on the Private topology?
2) Do you need packet-level controls (ACLs/iptables rules) or a high-level map (gateway, NAT, egress filter) with sample rule descriptions?

Plan: Kimberly will assemble the diagram; Mina will draft the narrative and the short routing/fallback summary; I'll collate and deliver the bundle (diagram + short write-up + evidence index). Expect a draft by EOD Monday PST.

Attachment: planning note stub (will send full attachments in next message).

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Security Architecture | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0180

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>, Veridian Audit Team <audits@veridian.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Enclave-lane topology v2 + evidence index (draft)

Ruth / team,

Please find attached the draft visualization and a brief evidence index. High level notes included in the diagram callouts:
- Data plane (in orange): tenant inference workloads run in isolated compute pools. For Dedicated this is our reserved GPU cluster segmented by tenant VLANs; for Private this is customer VPC compute with our sidecar that enforces policy.
- Control plane (in blue): control messages (scheduling, model versioning, metrics) flow over TLS to our multi-tenant control plane endpoints. Control plane endpoints do not accept raw customer data payloads; we restrict what telemetry and metadata are sent.
- KMS boundary (green hatch): when customers opt for customer-managed keys we terminate key operations in a separate HSM-backed KMS cluster accessible only via mutually authenticated endpoints.
- Egress chokepoints: all outbound flows exit through policy-enforced egress gateways; per-tenant rules are enforced at the gateway and at the sidecar.

Attachments (zipped as stubs in this thread):
- enclave-lane-topology-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB) — one-page diagram with callouts
- soc2-evidence-index.xlsx (Excel, 45KB) — lists artifacts and canonical locations
- egress-filters-snippets.txt (TXT, 3KB) — examples of per-tenant egress ACL snippets (redacted)

A couple open items we flagged in the index for your SOC reviewer: fine-grained packet logs for Private edge nodes (we have aggregated logs but can produce flow-level captures on request) and a KMS attestation excerpt if you need it for the control-of-keys question.

Let us know if you'd like the diagram annotated with sequence numbers for the model routing/fallback flow — happy to add.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Security Architect | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: enclave-lane-topology-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
Attachment: soc2-evidence-index.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

From: Veridian Audit Team <audits@veridian.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: soc2-review@acme-security.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Enclave-lane topology v2 + evidence index (draft)

Kimberly / Karthik — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we were after. Quick follow-ups from our reviewer:
1) Could you add a small numbered flow overlay (1-5) that walks through a single inference request from the customer's VPC to token return — highlight where KV cache or prefixes may be reused across tenants (if applicable).
2) For Private deployments using customer-managed KMS, can you provide the attestation excerpt or pointer to the HSM policy doc (redacted OK) referenced in your index?

If you can place those two items in the same Drive folder and reply with the link, we'll mark the SOC 2 doc as "visual + narrative received" and proceed to the next control.

We'll accept the artifacts by Thursday EOD.

Regards,
Ruth Allen
Veridian Audit Team
